title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.37: Five Scripts for the New Syntax
preview_title: Alpha.37 in Five Scripts: Struct Literals, IsSet on Properties, unset as NULL
description: One runnable script per alpha.37 change, each built around a pattern the change makes pleasant: POINT(10, 20) literals passed straight into PtInRect, IsSet(obj.prop) for optional settings and feature detection, unset as a null pointer for Win32 size queries and skipped outputs, Int32 instances passed by value and Struct.At as an address carrier, and a Pipeline class whose hooks default to unset. Plus the five pitfalls hit while writing them and the fork fix for a throwing getter that upstream reports as UnsetError.
preview: Five tested scripts, one per alpha.37 change, with the alpha.36 behaviour in the comments and the pitfalls found along the way.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.36: Objects That View Memory, and Three Errors That Finally Fire
preview_title: Alpha.36: ObjCreateWithDataPtr, Invalid base., #Import Clashes
description: Three short scripts for alpha.36: ObjCreateWithDataPtr turning an ordinary class into a Pixel view over an RGBA buffer, RegExMatchInfo() and friends throwing Invalid base. instead of crashing, and AhkLibPath and #Import clashes caught at load.
preview: ObjCreateWithDataPtr views, constructor calls that throw instead of crash, and #Import clashes caught at load, plus two bugs the fork fixed before shipping.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.35: Strict Keys and a Search Path That Follows the File
preview_title: Alpha.35: Float Keys Throw, #Include Follows the File, AhkLibPath
description: Three short scripts for alpha.35: a Map that throws on a Float key instead of storing a second one, #Include <Name> resolved from the including file's directory so tools\Fmt.ahk needs no Lib folder, and AhkLibPath switching a child script's library set per process.
preview: Float keys throw, the include search path follows the including file, and AhkLibPath swaps library sets per process: three tested scripts.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.34: Hidden Properties, Anonymous Unions, Typed NumPut
preview_title: Alpha.34: Enumerable: false, union { }, and NumPut(Int32, ...)
description: Three tested scripts for alpha.34: a Record class whose dirty flag and version hide from Props() but stay own properties, DefineProp finally rejecting a typo in the descriptor, a tagged union over one four-byte slot plus Win32's INPUT declared the way the C header reads, and a layout table of numeric classes that drives both NumPut and NumGet with no size column. Three pitfalls at the end: in is reserved, UIntPtr does not exist, and Format with nested braces.
preview: Hidden properties, anonymous unions and numeric classes in NumPut, each as a small pattern you can lift.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.33: Modules Get Local Imports and References
preview_title: Alpha.33: #Import Inside Functions, &Module.Var, and the Heap Bug It Shipped With
description: Three short scripts for alpha.33: #Import scoped to a function, &Module.Var handed to ByRef and SplitPath, and two former crashes caught as errors, plus the heap bug upstream shipped in &Module.Var.
preview: Local imports, references to module variables, and a heap-corruption bug that upstream alpha.33 shipped with.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.32: One Property, Three Fixes
preview_title: Alpha.32: Gui.FontHandle, With a 32-Bit Catch
description: The smallest release in the series gets one script: Gui.FontHandle read through GetObject before any control exists, the same handle on a new Edit, a second Gui's Text control borrowing it through WM_SETFONT, and the (g.FontHandle?) ?? fallback for older engines. Plus the catch that FontHandle is a UInt32 while WM_GETFONT returns the handle sign-extended, so compare the low 32 bits.
preview: One tested script for Gui.FontHandle, the three fixes in a paragraph, and a sign-extension pitfall worth knowing.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.31: Modules Export Everything
preview_title: Alpha.31 in Five Scripts: Implied Export, Facades, a #Module AHK Prelude
description: Alpha.31 removed the export keyword and made every module-level name public, with a leading underscore to hide helpers from {*} and #Import Export to forward an import. Five tested scripts show the new model as patterns: a library module, closed and open facades over one core, a project prelude in #Module AHK now that imports resolve there, unset values that survive two import hops, and the struct-view, split-property and virtual-reference fixes. Each before-claim was re-run on an alpha.30 engine, and the breaking change is listed by symptom.
preview: The export keyword is gone and modules export everything; five scripts turn the new rules into patterns, with the alpha.30 behaviour re-run beside each one.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.30: Void Returns and Three Removals
preview_title: Alpha.30 in Four Scripts: Void, (a?)(), Typed Struct Classes, Small Fixes
description: Four tested scripts for alpha.30: GetLocalTime and a CallbackCreate handler with the new "Void" return type, an emitter with optional hooks written as (cb?)(item) now that a?.() is gone, a Record struct migrated from i32 strings and bare sizes to Int32 and Int8[4] with its padding made visible, and the String(), StrGet(buf, 0), unset-through-&ref and Class.Base fixes as a Describe helper and a TryParse. Plus three things the parser taught me along the way.
preview: Four scripts for the release that added "Void" and removed a?.(), i32 type strings and bare-size struct fields.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.29: When Nothing Is a Value
preview_title: Alpha.29 in Three Scripts: Maybe Operator, Unset Returns, Unset Built-ins
description: Three tested scripts for alpha.29's unset semantics: optional parameters flowing through arithmetic and comparisons with one trailing ??, a finder that returns nothing instead of a sentinel, fat-arrow wrappers that pass a blank return through, and a prototype-chain walk, a regex tokenizer and a CallIfPresent helper built on built-ins that now return unset. Plus the five parser rules I tripped over, including why `missing? + 1` does not load.
preview: Three scripts for the release that made unset mean something: the maybe operator through every operator, unset returns, and unset from built-ins.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.28: #Requires Decides What "Nothing" Means
preview_title: Alpha.28 in Four Scripts: unset vs "", UnsetItemError, Opaque Handles
description: Four tested scripts for alpha.28. #Requires v2.1 switches a file to v2.1 mode, where a bare return and every silent built-in give no value instead of "", and ?? tells the two apart; #DefaultReturn is gone. A sparse [1, unset, 3] array raises UnsetItemError for its hole while a bad index stays IndexError. A fieldless struct becomes a typed window handle through StructClass.At, and a struct view over a buffer with a nested POINT works again. Plus a ByRef alias to a global surviving recursion and an OnMessage callback declining a message with a bare return.
preview: The v2.1 mode switch moves into #Requires, empty container slots get their own error, and a struct with no fields becomes a typed handle.

title: AutoHotkey v2.1-alpha.27: Structs Become One Block of Memory
preview_title: Alpha.27 in Three Scripts: Nested Structs, Reliable Destructors, Frozen Base
description: Three tested scripts for the alpha.27 struct changes. A RECT made of two POINTs is one allocation whose pointer goes straight into OffsetRect and SetRect, and a RECT2[3] array walks with a 16-byte stride. A Brush struct that calls DeleteObject in __Delete is released on time, including every element of a Brush[2], thanks to the destructor fixes. And the new Base guards: what `a.Base := b` now rejects, and how `struct Labeled extends POINT` gives the same result at definition time.
preview: Nested structs embedded in one block, destructors that run for every array element, and a Base you can no longer swap.

title: Sixteen New Models: GPT-6.1 Sol Joins the Perfect-Eval Club for 35 Cents
preview_title: GPT-6.1 Sol Aces AHK-Eval; Three Reasoners Run Out of Tokens
description: Sixteen new models on AHK-Eval, AHK-Contract, AHK-Repair and the esoteric probe. GPT-6.1 Sol passes all 181 hidden Eval cases, fixes 29 of 30 Repair items and solves 13 of 13 esoteric tasks, all for $0.35. Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash miss one shared date case. Eight models write a typed Struct on one line that AutoHotkey won't load. Fourteen of sixteen fail one repair item, thirteen of them by keeping m.Value, which AHK v2's match object doesn't have. GLM-5.3 Prime, Mistral Large 4 and Qwen3.8 Max Prime often reason past a 16,000- to 20,000-token cap without writing code.
preview: GPT-6.1 Sol: 36/36 and 181/181 on Eval for 35 cents. Gemini 4 Argon is one case behind with no reasoning. Three expensive reasoners spend their token budget thinking and never write the code.

title: How to Benchmark LLMs on AHK v2: Ten Rules From Nine Experiments
preview_title: The AHK v2 Benchmarking Playbook
description: Nine experiments on this blog graded LLM-written AutoHotkey v2 nine different ways: a GUI that must open, a transform toolkit, 36 hidden-test functions, four harness arms, 24 class contracts, a repair suite, a rare-feature probe, a classifier that tried to be the grader, and a grading graph that audited the grader. This post distills them into ten rules, each with the number that forced it. Run the code against hidden cases (a 95 code score crashed; a judge model passed 199 of 211 zero-pass scripts). Split the work into small independent tasks (parse failures fell from 35% to 2%). Prove the suite before any model sees it (48 mutants killed, a blind spec-read). Aim at v2 semantics, not algorithms. Measure the harness separately (a rules card is worth +0.4 tasks, self-tests +5.4). Never trust one board, freeze the protocol, and audit your own instruments.
preview: Ten rules for grading LLM-written AHK v2, each one forced by a number from the series' own boards.

title: Claude Opus 5.5: Every Answer Right, Eleven Answers Missing
preview_title: Opus 5.5 Aces AHK-Contract, Loses Eval Tasks to a Refusal Gate
description: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, run cold over the direct API, solves every AHK-Eval task it answers (33 of 33, 166 of 166 hidden cases), posts a perfect 24/24 on AHK-Contract, and fixes 27 of 30 AHK-Repair items for third place. What it doesn't answer, it never saw: a 'cyber' safety classifier blocked 16 of 103 prompts before the model wrote a token, on tasks like swapping letter case and converting hex. The gate is not deterministic, since five prompts passed on an unchanged retry, and it blocks email extraction as a fresh Eval task while letting the same work through as a Repair item.
preview: 33 of 33 answered Eval tasks solved, 24/24 on Contract, 27/30 on Repair, for about $1. Eleven tasks never reached the model: a safety classifier blocked them first.

title: Jev: A Model That Cannot Write Code, Grading 2,952 AHK v2 Scripts for 13 Cents
preview_title: Jev, OpenRouter's Decisions Model, Tries to Judge the AHK Bench
description: OpenRouter's new decisions model returns probabilities instead of text, so it cannot take the bench — but it can try to grade it. This post walks the undocumented /api/alpha/decisions schema, calls it from a forty-line AHK v2 class, and then sends every submission on AHK-Eval, AHK-Contract and AHK-Repair plus a 13-task rare-feature probe through it: 2,952 scripts, three questions each, $0.13. Jev predicts whether code loads with an AUROC of 0.82 and its low-confidence tail is reliable — every script it rated under 0.1 failed. But on whether code is correct it clears the always-say-yes baseline by under two points, rates 94% of zero-pass scripts as passing, would rank GPT-6 Astra thirteenth, and orders best-of-N candidates worse than a shuffle. Five charts show why: the failures it cannot see are fluent code calling a standard library AutoHotkey does not have.
preview: How the decisions API works, an AHK v2 client for it, and 2,952 graded scripts' worth of evidence that Jev is a reject filter, not a judge.

title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra: The First Perfect AHK-Eval, and the Bug It Refused to Fix
preview_title: GPT-6 Astra Runs the Table on AHK-Eval and AHK-Contract
description: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is the first model to post a perfect cold arm on AHK-Eval — 36/36 tasks, 181/181 hidden cases, at default reasoning effort with a 138-token median completion — and it repeats the feat at xhigh effort for three times the money and nothing else. It also clears AHK-Contract 24/24 with every hidden case passing, and fixes 28 of 30 AHK-Repair items with the highest hidden-case count the suite has recorded. The two it misses are the same task, broken the same way: asked to make the smallest change to someone else's code, it preserves a string comparison that AHK v2 throws on — the exact idiom it sidesteps when writing from scratch.
preview: 36/36, 24/24, 28/30 — a $1.33 sweep, and one repair item that shows where 'smallest change' stops being the right instruction.

title: Ox Alpha: The Syntax Is Perfect, the Standard Library Is Invented
preview_title: Ox Alpha Writes Clean AHK v2 Against a Library That Doesn't Exist
description: A cloaked, free stealth model on OpenRouter runs all three suites: 33/36 on AHK-Eval, 19/30 on AHK-Repair, 19/24 on AHK-Contract, with 59 of 60 eval and contract submissions parsing clean. Almost nothing it got wrong was a reasoning error. It reaches for Array.Sort, Array.Join and .Length() — the JavaScript standard library — and escapes quotes C#-style. Five repair calls that hit the 16k output cap all failed, one of them 509 seconds of invisible deliberation that left the original bug in place and bolted on a MsgBox.
preview: 59 of 60 parse clean, and the misses concentrate into four namable lookups rather than capability gaps.

title: Grok 4.6: Third on Everything, and a Share of the Eval Record
preview_title: Grok 4.6 Takes Third on All Three Suites
description: xAI's Grok 4.6 ran all three suites with ninety clean returns and zero parse failures on eval and repair: 35/36 on AHK-Eval — the joint-highest cold score at the time — 22/30 on AHK-Repair with the tightest minimality in its bracket, and 22/24 on AHK-Contract. The one eval miss is AE_NaturalSort, a structurally correct comparator that compares digit runs as strings. The contract parse failure is the round's most sophisticated mistake: the alpha.30 Struct keyword with the right types on one comma-separated line.
preview: No suite it wins, none where it leaves the top three — and one integer comparison from a perfect board.

title: Gemini 3.7 Flash: The Repair Board Gets a New Ceiling
preview_title: Gemini 3.7 Flash Fixes 28 of 30 for 27 Cents
description: Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash runs ninety calls for $0.27 at about four seconds each and takes rank 1 on AHK-Repair (28/30, five items clear of the previous best) and rank 1 on AHK-Contract with the suite's first perfect 24/24, while landing 33/36 on AHK-Eval with no zero-case tasks. Median completions around a thousand tokens and zero cap hits make it directly comparable to every historical arm.
preview: Rank 1 on repair, the first perfect contract sheet, and a bill of twenty-seven cents.

title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813: A Flawless Mid-Tier and a Reasoning Budget That Runs Out
preview_title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 Sweeps Easy and Mid, Then Reasons Past Its Budget
description: The GA checkpoint of DeepSeek V4 Pro, 2.7× cheaper than its predecessor, solves every easy and every mid task on AHK-Eval and then loses half the hard tier: 30/36, +8 over the undated model. On AHK-Repair (14/30) and AHK-Contract (20/24) it is a heavy reasoner that runs out of room — a 15,312-token median against a 16,000 cap, two calls that produced no code at all, and a harness fallback that wrote the reasoning transcript into an .ahk file.
preview: 12/12 easy, 12/12 mid, 6/12 hard — and half the repair suite bound by its own reasoning budget.

title: The Grading Graph: One Rule, Four Tiers, and 47 Scripts That Quietly Did Nothing
preview_title: The Harness Graph — and the Silent Bug It Found in 47 Scripts
description: The grading harness behind the benchmarks, drawn in full: four gated tiers, one shared resource that forces the live-input tier to run serially, and a checker whose only job is discarding untrustworthy evidence. Pointed at the 159-script AHK-Eval corpus it found 49 files that will not load and 47 that load perfectly and silently do nothing — Clipboard := text is v1, so in v2 the copy never happens. Two fixes to CodeIntel cut the noise 45% while raising the count of scripts with a real defect from 1 to 48.
preview: A dependency graph, a shim that shadows the built-ins, and a clipboard benchmark full of scripts that cannot copy.

title: Opus 5 Under the Live Harness: The First 100
preview_title: Opus 5 Takes the Clipboard Board's First Perfect Score
description: Claude Opus 5, run as the live working harness rather than a cold API call, takes rank 1 of 83 on the clipboard-formatter benchmark with the first perfect static score the board has produced — 100/100, a running window, and a 20/20 fully dark render. The two points over Fable 5 come from one item: a third derived wrapper class, where each override gives Value a different meaning per control type. The run also exposed a defect in the capture harness — PowerShell is DPI-unaware, so every screenshot of a DPI-aware window was measured 20% small and silently cropped, including the previously published rank-1 shot.
preview: A perfect 100 at the top, and the discovery that the board's screenshots were cropping 20% off every DPI-aware window.

title: Kimi K3: Four Tasks Better Than K2.6, and the First Model Through AHK-Contract
preview_title: Kimi K3 Nearly Beats the Agent Benchmark Cold
description: Moonshot K3 takes rank 6 on AHK-Eval at 34/36 — four tasks clear of K2.6 — and becomes the first model ever to run AHK-Contract, scoring 23/24 cold. It went 4/4 on the binding and meta categories the suite named its load-bearing cases, leaving one task of headroom for the cold-to-agent delta the benchmark was built to measure. Its single contract loss is one line: calling a stored hook as this.pre(v), which AHK resolves as a method call and hands the instance as an implicit first argument. Both sweeps, 60 calls, $1.71.
preview: 23/24 cold on a suite built to be beaten by agents — and the one miss is a method-call resolution bug.

title: AHK-Repair: Terra Fixes What It Can't Write
preview_title: AHK-Repair: Terra Tops the Fix Board
description: Thirty real broken submissions mined from the AHK-Eval failure corpus become a repair benchmark: fix another model's dead code with the smallest change, graded against the original hidden cases plus a minimality metric. Eleven models ran it for $3.45 total. GPT-5.6 Terra — the terse mid-tier that drops easy generation tasks — is the best repairer at 64%; GLM-5.2 repairs better than GLM-5 while scoring worse on generation; parse deaths get fixed at 40%, silent wrong-value bugs at 28%. Seven bugs survived everyone, including Terra's own submission for a task it fixed from another model's pen.
preview: Terra repairs 64% of other models' dead code — including a task its own submission still fails.

title: AHK-Contract: 24 Class Contracts, 173 Hidden Tests, and a Benchmark Built to Be Beaten by Agents
preview_title: AHK-Contract: The OOP Benchmark
description: AHK-Eval grades one stateless call; it can't see construction protocol, super chaining, dispatch order, this-binding, or lifecycle. AHK-Contract can: 24 class contracts across six categories, 173 hidden behavioral cases with base-chain error matching, graded on the pinned alpha.30 fork. Adversarially gated before any model run — 48 plausible-wrong mutants all killed, blind spec-reads on every task, shuffled-order re-grading. Two arms: cold one-shot vs coding agent with execution feedback; the per-category delta is the product. Three falsifiable predictions frozen in advance.
preview: 24 class contracts, 173 hidden tests, zero models so far — the cold-vs-agent delta is the product.

title: Meta Muse Spark 1.1: Mid-Board Debut, Three Tasks Dead on One Invented Method
preview_title: Muse Spark 1.1 Debuts at #12
description: Meta's first paid-API model runs AHK-Eval three days after launch: 30/36, rank 12 of 28, tying Kimi K2.6 on tasks and losing the tiebreak on hidden cases. Strings and regex swept clean; the data category collapsed to 3/6 on a single invented Array.Sort() across three tasks. Plus the quietest failure the suite has recorded — DateAdd's "Months" unit silently parsing as minutes — and a hard task lost to the 8,000-token reasoning cliff. Total sweep: $0.35.
preview: Meta's first paid-API model ties Kimi K2.6 at 30/36 — and loses three tasks to one invented .Sort() call.

title: OpenAI GPT-5.6: A New #1 by One Hidden Case — and a Family That Codes in Borrowed APIs
description: All six GPT-5.6 endpoints ran AHK-Eval on launch day. Sol Pro dethrones GPT-5.5 by a single hidden case (177 vs 176); $6/M Luna Pro ties $30/M Sol at 34/36 and lands on the cost-efficiency frontier; Terra Pro pays 6× the tokens to score below base Terra. Nearly every dropped task is a borrowed API — s.Split(), Array.Sort(), a nonexistent Trunc(), and the char-range comparison that cost the new #1 its only task. Total sweep: $5.23.

title: xAI Grok 4.5: Fourth Place, Undone by Borrowed Operators
description: xAI's newest lands fourth of eighteen on the 36-task hidden-test suite — 31/36 cold, the best xAI run recorded, with a perfect easy tier only GPT-5.5 matches and a hard tier that ties Kimi K2.6. Every dropped point traces to an idiom from another language: infix % for Mod(), an invented Array.Sort(), and one InStr call with its arguments in the wrong slots that aced RFC-4180 quote escapes but lost the task to plain comma-splitting. Total run cost: 32 cents.

title: Tencent Hy3: One Option String From a Window
description: Tencent's 295B MoE joins the clipboard-formatter board on both its paid and free endpoints: a +41-point generational jump over Hunyuan A13B, a static score of 87 tying GLM-4.7 and GPT-OSS 120B — and two startup crashes, each exactly one corrected line away from a working window. Compared against the open MoE cohort and the closed budget tier at the same price. Updated same day with AHK-Eval results: 19/36 and 22/36 on the hidden-test suite — mid-field, with the free endpoint tying GPT-5.1's cold run and beating the paid endpoint by three tasks.

title: Poolside Laguna XS 2.1: The Coding Agent That Writes AHK v1
description: The board's first Poolside entry: a 33B-A3B coding-agent model that fails the parse gate on both endpoints — not with v2 mistakes, but with a confident v1/JavaScript hybrid dialect. Its static 50 still tops the sub-50B open class and beats closed GPT-5.4 mini by 18 points, while GPT-5.4 nano proves small-and-cheap can ship a running window. Updated same day with AHK-Eval results: 8/36 and 9/36 — the floor of the 17-model hidden-test board, with regex mid-field and strings at zero.

title: AHK-Eval Round 3: Self-Tests, and What Happens When the Harness Is Real
description: Two final harness arms: models writing their own test cases lift the field +5.4 tasks (GPT-5.5 posts the first non-Fable perfect run; one model regresses on its own wrong tests) — and headless Claude Code turns Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 from 29 and 25 cold into 36/36 and 35/36, at eleven cents a task.

title: AHK-Eval Round 2: What a Coding Harness Is Actually Worth
description: The same 36 tasks and 181 hidden tests, re-run with two harness arms across all 13 models: a rules-card system prompt moves the field +0.4 tasks and hurts as many models as it helps; one round of execution feedback lifts every single model (+3.3 mean) and carries Fable 5 to the suite's first perfect 36/36 — after it wrote its favorite trap yet again.

title: AHK-Eval: 36 Tasks, 181 Hidden Tests, 13 Models
description: A HumanEval-style AHK v2 benchmark: 36 independent functions across six categories and three difficulty tiers, graded against hidden test cases. GPT-5.5 lands one task from perfect; Claude Fable 5 — the model that built the benchmark, run cold over the bare API — takes second at 34/36 and falls into its own favorite trap.

title: Claude Fable 5: Five Entries, Five Windows
description: Claude Fable 5 joins the clipboard-formatter board with five entries under five harness configs — and sweeps both gates: all five parse, all five run. Two ship fully dark 20/20 windows; the bare no-tooling entry is the leanest runner on the board at 40 lines. Updated July 1: a sixth run under the full live harness clears the whole checklist at 98 and takes rank 1 on the board.

title: The Clipboard Toolkit: 11 Coding Models, 12 Transforms
description: A second, deliberately discriminating AHK v2 benchmark: twelve independent clipboard text transforms, graded functionally against hidden test cases. The top-11 coding models spread from 3/12 to 11/12 — with the best logic in the field (Opus 4.8) hung on a crashing GUI.

title: One Prompt, 77 Models: An AHK v2 Clipboard-Formatter Benchmark
description: 77 LLMs answered the same strict AHK v2 prompt, graded on two signals — does it parse, and does it actually run — against the alpha.30 fork, with per-model pages and live OpenRouter sweeps. Only 30 of the 74 that returned code build a working window — Claude Fable 5's five entries all do.

title: Claude Opus 4.8: AHK v2 Output Examples
description: Real, unedited AHK v2 outputs from Claude Opus 4.8 -- idiomatic Map() usage, correct event-callback binding, validated properties, typed error handling, and v2.1 alpha struct overlays. Includes a runnable clipboard-history example.

title: CloudAHK: Remote AHK v2 Execution via REST API
description: A FastAPI service for executing AHK v2 scripts over HTTP with an ANTLR parser endpoint. Includes an AHK v2 client class and template system.

title: AHK v2.1 Alpha Tricks: Unions, Arenas, and Prototype Black Magic
description: Advanced patterns combining struct unions, typed callbacks, DefineProp, and Struct.At -- IEEE 754 dissection, ring buffers, arena allocators, Vec2 math, and dynamic class factories.

title: AHK v2.1-alpha.26: Memory Optimization and Modal Dialog Fixes
description: Struct memory co-allocation for faster construction, array alignment fixes, keyboard shortcuts in modal dialogs, and WM_CLOSE reload.

title: AHK v2.1-alpha.25: Inline Window Options and Stability Fixes
description: The ahk_opt WinTitle criterion for per-call window search options, hotkey behavior fixes, and module system improvements.

title: AHK v2.1-alpha.24: Typed Callbacks and C-Style Unions
description: CallbackCreate with typed parameter arrays for float support, DefineProp Offset for union-like memory overlays, and wildcard re-exports.

title: AHK v2.1-alpha.23: Numeric Types and Struct Arrays
description: Dedicated numeric type classes (Int32, Float32), structured arrays with StructClass[N] syntax, negative indexing, and Size fix.

title: AHK v2.1-alpha.22: The Struct Revolution
description: The native Struct keyword with typed fields, auto-generated .Ptr classes, DefineProp() function, Type() unset, and Win32 API integration.

title: Object-Oriented Programming in LLMs
description: How large language models understand and generate OOP code, patterns they excel at, and leveraging their capabilities for better AHK v2 class design.

title: Building OOP GUIs in AutoHotkey v2
description: A comprehensive guide to creating maintainable, reusable GUI applications using object-oriented principles and component architecture.

title: Creating Dark Mode GUIs in AHK v2
description: Step-by-step tutorial on implementing native dark mode theming using DllCall and Windows API integration.

title: Customizing TapHoldManager.ahk
description: Master the TapHoldManager library for creating sophisticated key combinations with tap, hold, multi-tap, and tap-and-hold behaviors.

title: Prompt Engineering for AHK v2 Code Generation
description: Craft effective prompts to get high-quality AutoHotkey v2 code from LLMs with templates, anti-patterns, and validation techniques.

title: Using AutoHotkey v2 with Coding Agents and LLMs
description: A lightweight workflow for combining AutoHotkey v2 scripts with GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, and other coding agents.
